question: What is the name of the geostationary satellite launched by ISRO in 1983 that provides high power TV broadcasting and telecommunications national coverage transponders?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Insat-1B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **INSAT-1B** stands as a significant** component of the Indian National Satellite System (INSAT),** a communications satellite launched in **1983** by the** Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• Manufactured by **Ford Aerospace**, INSAT-1B was deployed from the payload bay of the** Space Shuttle Challenger** and commenced operations in October 1983.
 
• This satellite orbits at a longitude of 74 degrees east, with a speed of 3.07 kilometers per second and an altitude of 35,786 kilometers.
 
• It features a visual channel with a resolution of 2.75 kilometers and an IR channel with a resolution of 11 kilometers.
 
• INSAT-1B is equipped with a data channel designated for relaying meteorological, hydrological, and oceanographic data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bhaskara-I and II **were two satellites developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), serving as India's first low-Earth orbit Earth observation satellites.
 
• **GSAT-7**, alternatively known as INSAT-4F or Rukmini, is a multi-band military communications satellite crafted by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
 
• **Radar Imaging Satellite 1,** abbreviated as **RISAT-1,** was an Indian remote sensing satellite engineered and managed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
